note: Thursday 5 Nov 2026 07:02 SGT run. Fear & Greed jumped to 31/Fear (from 19/Extreme Fear) as Wednesday's midterm-relief rally (VIX -20.3% to 16.61, S&P +1.58%, Dow +3.03%) cleared election-uncertainty hedging -- Stock Price Strength flipped to Greed (61) while Safe-Haven Demand and Junk Bond Demand stayed deeply fearful (1, 12), a genuine mixed read rather than a clean all-clear. Breadth was broad on the day itself (NYSE advancers led ~2.6:1) but slower-moving gauges (52-wk highs/lows, 50-DMA breadth) had not yet caught up as of the last available prints. Global fund flows remain stuck on the week-ending-Oct-28 cut -- the week-ending-Nov-4 release (first to capture the midterm result and Wednesday's rally) is still due Thu/Fri Nov 5-6.

flows.period: week ending Wed Oct 28 2026 (EPFR/Lipper via Reuters + BofA Flow Show) -- still the latest published cut as of this run
flows.narrative: No newer weekly global fund-flow cut has published since week-ending-Oct-28; the week-ending-Nov-4 cut (due Thu/Fri Nov 5-6) genuinely had not posted yet at 07:02 SGT Thursday. A search initially surfaced an attractive 'week through Nov 5' Lipper print but direct verification showed it was dated November 2025, a year-old false match reusing near-identical seasonal language, and was discarded. The still-latest real cut (week ending Oct 28) showed global equity funds +$56.2B (BofA) entirely via passive ETF buying (+$75.9B) against an active-fund outflow (-$19.6B), China the standout at +$25.7B-equivalent, Europe at -$2.3B (worst since July), and gold funds' first outflow since July (-$1.7B); none of this reflects the subsequent AI-capex shock, VIX spike, crude crash, midterm week or Wednesday's relief rally.
